subject: Update: Rivera7b timeout wave — mitigation & recovery plan
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Retail Ops <ops@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Evan Torres <evan.torres@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: elevated timeouts for Rivera7b impacting inference calls

Hi Evan / Acme Ops team,

We wanted to let you know we're seeing an elevated rate of timeout (502/504) responses for requests routed to Rivera7b starting ~08:55 PDT this morning. A subset of requests is experiencing retries and increased latency. At the moment the impact to your tenant is approximately 3-7% of gen requests (we'll refine numbers below).

What we're doing now:
- Routing policy: automatic fallback to Rivera7b-light for short requests to reduce failures.
- Short-term throttling for large-sequence requests to protect overall throughput.
- Ops runbook: collecting KV cache and per-shard logs; attaching a small log snippet for visibility.

Attachments: [rivera7b-log-snippet.txt (text)]

Immediate ask from you:
- If you have critical batches or scheduled jobs hitting Rivera7b, please pause or reroute to Rivera7b-light for the next 2 hours.
- Share any recent payload changes (not required immediately) that we should correlate.

We'll provide an update by 12:30 PDT with our short-term mitigation and any ETA for a recovery. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Ben / Monica / Rishi,

Looping you in — Acme started reporting visible 504s ~09:20; they call out long-document workloads (~3k tokens). I pushed our initial fallback and throttles and shared the log snippet.

Summary of what's happening (ops telemetry):
- Error class: intermittent 502/504 from the transformer worker pool for Rivera7b.
- Pattern: spikes correlate with >2.5k token requests, higher KV cache churn on those calls.
- Impact: ~3–8% of requests for Acme tenant during measured window; global impact lower (~1.2%).

Immediate asks:
- Monica: can you confirm whether any recent kernel change or memory-pressure rollout occurred on Rivera GPU pool since 08:00?
- Rishi: can you validate if the compiler's FP16 kernel fallback engaged for long-context paths?
- Ben: please prep a short customer-friendly update (one-pager) we can push after we have mitigation confirmation.

I'll keep Acme in the loop.

Kim
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Aug 2028 10:58:00 -0700
Subject: Rivera7b telemetry + mitigation status

Team,

Quick update from infra: we confirmed a recent micro-kernel rollback that was auto-promoted at 07:45 PDT to Rivera-serving nodes; the rollback changed the memory alignment heuristics for KV cache pages. For short requests this is fine, but for >2k token workloads it increases fragmentation and caused occasional worker restarts under load.

Actions taken (10:00–10:45):
- Reverted that rollback and re-applied the stable kernel profile to Rivera GPU pool (verified on 60% of nodes).
- Increased prefix-KV cache retention for Rivera7b to reduce thrash for long contexts.
- Adjusted autoscaler thresholds to spin up extra workers for the next 90 minutes.

Preliminary result: the 504 rate for Acme's tenant dropped from ~6.3% to ~1.1% in a 15-minute window following changes. We'll continue to monitor.

Uploads: rivera7b-mitigation-checklist.md (operational steps taken).

Next steps:
- Continue full rollout of stable kernel tonight (target 18:00 PDT).
- Drafting postmortem; Ben, please coordinate customer-facing language. Rishi, save the KV cache heap dumps for analysis.

Monica
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: rivera7b-mitigation-checklist.md]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Retail Ops <ops@acmeretail.com>, Evan Torres <evan.torres@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Aug 2028 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Resolved: Rivera7b timeout wave — recovery & next steps

Evan / Acme team,

Update: Rivera7b routing has returned to normal and we've seen error rates return to baseline for your tenant. Timeline and summary: 
- Root cause: an auto-promoted kernel rollback altered KV cache alignment on Rivera-serving nodes, increasing fragmentation and causing intermittent worker restarts under long-context load.
- Mitigation: full stable kernel profile rollback completed to 95% of Rivera pool by 13:40 PDT, KV retention tuning, and temporary autoscaler capacity bump.
- Impact: peak user-visible errors between 08:55–11:30 PDT; peak error rate for Acme was ~6.7%. Post-mitigation rolling average is <0.5%.

What we recommend for you:
- Continue routing long-document jobs to Rivera7b-light for the next 24 hours if possible while we finish validation.
- We'll share a customer-facing postmortem draft by tomorrow 10:00 PDT (attached is the working draft).

Attachments: [rivera7b-postmortem-draft.pdf (pdf)]

Ben will follow up with the finalized postmortem and any credit proposals (if applicable). Apologies for the disruption — let us know if you want a short sync to walk through technical details.

Thanks for your patience,
Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
